limits: Introductory survey-style chapter: no experiments, one anecdotal prompt comparison, no authors named in the text.
Many figures (1.7T parameters, $63 million) are estimates without citation.

Some statements are loose or wrong: 'In 2024, OpenAI released GPT-4' (it is 2023); LoRA glossed as 'low-rank approximations' (it is low-rank adaptation) and said to optimise the network architecture; BPE example merges 'appl' as a token, which is illustrative only.
Model landscape is dated to early-mid 2024 (GPT-4o, Claude 3, Llama 3).
Next-token generation is described as picking the most likely word, ignoring sampling and temperature.
practices: Compare models by running the same prompt across several models and reading the responses (Model Comparison).
Use token counts, not word counts, to manage model processing limits (Models for Text Generation).
Use human oversight because training data carries biases (Historical Underpinnings).
Do not input sensitive data when a provider may use it for retraining or fine-tuning (Summary).
